blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's verified local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live listing feed or board statistics are attached to this page yet.

Park Royal is the MLS sub-area around the Park Royal shopping centre at Marine Drive and Taylor Way — West Vancouver's eastern gateway, at the foot of the Lions Gate Bridge and the mouth of the Capilano River. The centre opened in 1950, is presented by the centre as Canada's first covered shopping mall, operates as North and South malls divided by Marine Drive, and is classified in the District's OCP as West Vancouver's regional shopping centre.
This guide covers Park Royal's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Condo buildings in Park Royal

Municipal / reserve split, flagged first because it governs everything in this sub-area: Park Royal straddles a tenure boundary — part of the shopping centre lands sit on Capilano Indian Reserve No. 5 (X̱wemelch'stn), Squamish Nation land, held under the Park Royal Lease (indenture dated April 1, 1974), where the Squamish Nation exercises land-use and zoning control; the rest is District of West Vancouver municipal land under Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) and OCP Bylaw No. 4985 (2018). (The 2506/2220 bylaw pair belongs to White Rock only — never attribute it to West Vancouver.) Every property here needs its tenure confirmed on title before pricing or financing.
The WestRoyal — 328 Taylor Way and 338 Taylor Way

The sub-area's best-known condo development: two towers at Taylor Way beside Park Royal, built 1993 per the building directory and current listings, concrete, with an indoor pool, sauna, exercise centre, workshop and garden. The directory records its bylaws as "pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed with restrictions" — the rental-restriction element of that line is VOID since November 24, 2022. Current listings record Apartment/Condo form in the Park Royal sub-area, cats OK, and no age restriction — a listing calling a unit "perfect for downsizing" is marketing language, not a 55+ bylaw. Unit count: Not confirmed from the sources checked. Counted: 1 (one development across two addresses).
Evelyn by Onni — 768 Arthur Erickson Place (with residences also addressed on Arthur Erickson Place, including 788 and 866)

The terraced condo residences of the Evelyn masterplan above the Village at Park Royal: the building directory records Evelyn at 768 Arthur Erickson Place as built in 2019, with bike room, elevator, exercise centre, in-suite laundry, storage and wheelchair access; current listings record Apartment/Condo units at 768 (built 2019, concrete, concierge, sauna) and describe 866 Arthur Erickson Place units as "the Evelyn," with concierge, gym, sauna and guest suite. No source checked states any age restriction, and no published rental restriction is relied on here (any such line would be void in any event —). Unit count for the 768 building: Not confirmed from the sources checked — the wider Evelyn masterplan also contains detached houses (see below) and is not a single condo count. Counted: 1.

items.t: Park Royal is the MLS sub-area around the Park Royal shopping centre at Marine Drive and Taylor Way — West Vancouver's eastern gateway, at the foot of the Lions Gate Bridge and the mouth of the Capilano River. The centre opened in 1950, is presented by the centre as Canada's first covered shopping mall, operates as North and South malls divided by Marine Drive, and is classified in the District's OCP as West Vancouver's regional shopping centre.
Nearby areas: Ambleside (west), Dundarave (further west along Marine Drive), and — across the Capilano River in the District of North Vancouver — Norgate, Pemberton Heights and Lower Capilano.

Where condo stock concentrates: in and around the centre — the Evelyn residences on Arthur Erickson Place above the Village at Park Royal, the WestRoyal towers on Taylor Way, and the low-rise stock on the streets south of Marine Drive toward Ambleside, including Keith Road. Detached houses sit on the quiet streets south of Marine Drive.

Transit: Park Royal Exchange is the western terminus of the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus, which since September 7, 2026 runs one-seat through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station (roughly 5 a.m.–2 a.m., every 6–7 minutes at peak); the exchange is also the hub for West Vancouver's Blue Bus routes, including the 250/250A downtown–Horseshoe Bay/Dundarave service via the Lions Gate Bridge.

Schools: the nearest SD45 elementary schools are Irwin Park Elementary (K–7, 2455 Haywood Avenue) toward Ambleside/Dundarave and Westcot Elementary (K–7, 760 Westcot Road) at the foot of the British Properties; the east-side catchment secondary school is West Vancouver Secondary (Grades 8–12, 1750 Mathers Avenue). Confirm the catchment by exact address with West Vancouver Schools.

Recreation: Ambleside Park and the east end of the Centennial Seawalk are immediately east; Capilano River Regional Park runs up the canyon across the river, with the Cleveland Dam (completed 1954) and the Capilano River Hatchery (completed 1971; reported closed to the public for construction starting October 1, 2026, until further notice).
Health: the North Shore's hospital is Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver — across the Capilano River.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Park Royal

items.t: Density is in active transition here: on July 21, 2025 the Province issued ministerial directives requiring OCP amendments increasing density in the Park Royal–Taylor Way area by December 31, 2025; the District missed that deadline (and delivered 58 of its 220-unit year-one housing target), a provincial order effective April 7, 2026 implemented the neighbouring Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan, and the Park Royal–Taylor Way directive remains outstanding with quarterly provincial progress reports required through 2026 and 2027. Treat any density-based value claim for a specific parcel as not confirmed until an adopted bylaw names it.
Suites and coach houses: both are permitted in the District and require building permits, Zoning Bylaw s. 130 and BC Building Code compliance, and a business licence to operate as rentals.

District taxes and the additional school tax: municipal-side 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2 and a further 5% on September 2, 2026; water/sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly. The Province's additional school tax applies at West Vancouver values: 0.2% on the residential portion assessed between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027. Homes on reserve land are under a different tax/tenure regime — not confirmed per title.

blocks.text: Good to know about Park Royal

items.t: Canada's first covered shopping mall is also a First Nations leasehold story. Park Royal opened in 1950; part of its lands are Capilano IR No. 5 under a lease dated April 1, 1974, and on the reserve portion the Squamish Nation — not the District — is the zoning authority, with the District providing building design review and inspection so construction meets municipal standards.

The province has already overridden West Vancouver once, next door. When the District missed its December 31, 2025 directive deadlines, a provincial order effective April 7, 2026 amended the District's bylaw to implement the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan itself. The Park Royal–Taylor Way directive is the same instrument, still outstanding — buyers here are pricing inside an unresolved provincial process.

"Evelyn" is a masterplan, not a building. The counted condo entry is the 768 Arthur Erickson Place residences (built 2019); the same Arthur Erickson Place street also carries Evelyn detached houses built 2024/2025. Quoting "Evelyn" unit counts or ages without the civic address mixes two different products.

The additional school tax is a real carrying cost at these values. On top of District taxes: 0.2% on the assessed portion between $3M and $4M and 0.4% above $4M in 2026, rising to 0.3% / 0.6% on January 1, 2027 — a line item downsizers moving from a long-held house often meet for the first time.

The salmon hatchery across the river is closed for construction. The Capilano River Hatchery (completed 1971, normally ~250,000 visitors a year) was reported closed to the public starting October 1, 2026, until further notice — relevant to anyone buying on the river trails' amenity value this season.

West Vancouver's OCP moved again in December 2025. Council adopted OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 5406, 2025 on December 1, 2025 to align the OCP with the 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report — always cite the current consolidated Bylaw 4985, not the 2018 original, and never the White Rock 2506/2220 pair.

items.t: Park Royal is the MLS® sub-area around the Park Royal shopping centre at Marine Drive and Taylor Way — the District of West Vancouver's eastern gateway, at the foot of the Lions Gate Bridge and the mouth of the Capilano River. The centre opened in 1950, is presented by the centre as Canada's first covered shopping mall, operates as North and South malls divided by Marine Drive, and is classified in the District's OCP as West Vancouver's regional shopping centre.

Search names: "Park Royal," "Park Royal Village," "Marine Drive West Van," "Taylor Way," and street searches around Main Street, Keith Road (West Vancouver side) and the avenues south of Marine Drive.

Where attached stock concentrates: in and around the centre — the Evelyn residences on Arthur Erickson Place above the Village at Park Royal (apartment condos plus detached houses inside one masterplan), the WestRoyal towers on Taylor Way (apartment condos), and low-rise stock on the streets south of Marine Drive toward Ambleside, including Keith Road. Detached houses sit on the quiet streets south of Marine Drive.
Any individual listing's tenure must be verified, never assumed from the sub-area name.

Recreation and development-permit frame: Ambleside Park and the east end of the Centennial Seawalk are immediately west along the waterfront; Capilano River Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) runs up the Capilano Canyon across the river — the 91 m Cleveland Dam (completed 1954) at the park's head and Fisheries and Oceans Canada's Capilano River Hatchery (completed 1971, normally ~250,000 visitors a year; reported closed to the public for construction starting October 1, 2026, until further notice). The Park Royal Shopping Centre lands are a named Form & Character Development Permit area in the OCP, and foreshore and environmental DP rules apply along the waterfront and watercourses. The Lions Gate Bridge is at the sub-area's doorstep; no official drive-time figure is published — drive times not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Park Royal

items.t: Why this section is mostly a contrast section: The rules below are stated in full because the format requires them, because the sub-area's two counted apartment stratas are the stock a townhouse search actually lands on, and because the tenure check that replaces strata diligence here — freehold versus reserve leasehold — is the first-order rule for this ground.

Tenure check first (the Park Royal diligence order): confirm whether the property is freehold municipal land or a leasehold interest on Capilano IR No. 5, and if leasehold, get the head-lease terms, remaining term and any prepaid/rent-reset structure before pricing or financing discussions. Lenders treat reserve-land leaseholds individually — flag the tenure to the buyer's mortgage broker at the offer stage, not after subjects. Only after tenure is settled does the strata frame below apply, and it applies only to a freehold strata purchase.

District plans and zoning (District of West Vancouver): Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) and OCP Bylaw No. 4985 (2018) govern the municipal side; the OCP was amended again December 1, 2025 (OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 5406, 2025, aligning it with the 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report) — cite the current consolidated OCP, not the 2018 original. White Rock's Bylaw 2506 / 2220 pair belongs to White Rock only and is never cited for this ground. On Capilano IR No. 5, the Squamish Nation controls zoning under the Park Royal Lease arrangements. Suites and coach houses are both permitted in the District and require building permits, Zoning Bylaw s. 130 and BC Building Code compliance, and a business licence to operate as rentals.

Density is in active transition here: on July 21, 2025, the Province issued ministerial directives requiring West Vancouver to amend its OCP to increase density in the Park Royal–Taylor Way area (with defined minimum densities) and in single-family/duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave, and to adopt the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan — all by December 31, 2025. Treat any density-based value claim for a specific parcel as not confirmed until an adopted bylaw names it.

Evelyn masterplan — built houses inside a counted masterplan, NOT lots

Serviced position, District side: West Vancouver water/sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District — the serviced position for District lots as the District states it. Parcel-level servicing beyond that wording: Not confirmed; confirm the specific lot with the District.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel at Park Royal is documented, and no ALR split is stated — this is urban gateway ground on the research record. A specific parcel's ALR status is a per-parcel check on ALC mapping in any event.

blocks.text: Reserve side

items.t: Capilano IR No. 5 lands under the Park Royal Lease (indenture dated April 1, 1974): part of the shopping centre — and, per the research, leasehold residential interests to the south — sit on Squamish Nation land held under that lease. Under the arrangements documented in the Nation's zoning by-law amendments for the Park Royal leasehold lands, the Nation controls zoning on Capilano IR No. 5, while West Vancouver provides building design review and inspection services on the leasehold lands so construction meets municipal standards. A leasehold interest there is NOT a fee-simple lot: what is bought is the lease interest, on the head-lease terms, remaining term and any prepaid/rent-reset structure — confirm all three on title before pricing or financing, and flag the tenure to the mortgage broker at offer stage, because lenders treat reserve-land leaseholds individually. The exact set of residential parcels on reserve versus municipal land: Not verified — title-by-title.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Park Royal

items.t: Zoning — District Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010), District side only: secondary suites and coach houses are both permitted in the District and require building permits, Zoning Bylaw s.

Density in active transition — the Park Royal–Taylor Way directive: on July 21, 2025, the Province issued ministerial directives requiring West Vancouver to amend its OCP to increase density in the Park Royal–Taylor Way area (with defined minimum densities) and in single-family/duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave, and to adopt the Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan — all by December 31, 2025. The area's zoning is in active transition — treat any density-based value claim for a specific parcel as not confirmed until an adopted bylaw names it, and verify the current designation for the property.

Hazard and form-and-character development permits: the Park Royal Shopping Centre lands are a named Form & Character Development Permit area in the OCP, and foreshore and environmental DP rules apply along the waterfront and watercourses — the District's hazard/foreshore DP frame for this ground. Confirm whether a Foreshore Development Permit area applies to a waterfront-adjacent lot before promising renovation or subdivision scope.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Park Royal ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

District property taxes + additional school tax: municipal-side homes pay District of West Vancouver taxes — the 2026 payment was due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2 and a further 5% on September 2, 2026; roughly half of the tax bill is collected by the District for other taxing authorities, and water/sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly. The Province's additional school tax also bites at West Vancouver values: 0.2% on the residential portion assessed between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% on the portion above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027. Homes on reserve land are under a different tax/tenure regime — not confirmed per title.

Property transfer tax — worked example (inputs + tier math): on a $1,800,000 District-side freehold purchase, fully residential, no exemption — 1% on the first $200,000 ($2,000) + 2% on $200,000–$1,800,000 ($32,000) = $34,000. Anchors: $500K→$8,000; $1.0M→$18,000; $1.2M→$22,000; $1.5M→$28,000; $2.0M→$38,000; $3.5M→$93,000 INCLUDING the further 2% tier over $3M (tiers: 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000). Note: PTT treatment of a reserve-land leasehold differs from a freehold purchase — confirm with the buyer's lawyer/notary where tenure is leasehold.

faq.a: It depends on the parcel, and the two can be streets apart. Municipal-side homes are freehold under District bylaws; lands on Capilano IR No. 5 are leasehold under the 1974 Park Royal Lease, with the Squamish Nation controlling zoning. faq.q: Is a home near Park Royal freehold or leasehold?

faq.a: Two verified developments: The WestRoyal (328/338 Taylor Way, built 1993, two towers) and Evelyn by Onni on Arthur Erickson Place (768 recorded built 2019) above the Village at Park Royal. Everything else named in is detached houses inside the Evelyn masterplan, a developer-page proposal, a rental proposal, or a care residence.
faq.q: Which condo buildings are actually at Park Royal?

faq.a: Yes, long-term — the "rentals allowed with restrictions" element of its directory line is void province-wide since November 24, 2022. A strata can still restrict short-term rentals.
faq.q: Can I rent out a WestRoyal unit?

faq.a: No. Building sources record pets/rentals with restrictions and no age restriction; "downsizer" copy describes the likely buyer, not a bylaw. The legal test is a 55+ bylaw in the strata's filed bylaws — confirm on the Form B. Park Royal has zero verified 55+ ownership stock.
faq.q: Is the WestRoyal a 55+ building? A listing called it "perfect for downsizing."

faq.a: No. It is a rental retirement residence at 701–727 Keith Road (Independent Living, registered Assisted Living, Long-term Care, Memory Care). Nothing to buy.
faq.q: What is Amica Lions Gate — can I buy there?

faq.a: The attached ownership stock is two apartment-condo developments (The WestRoyal towers on Taylor Way; Evelyn on Arthur Erickson Place), plus detached houses.
faq.q: Are there any townhouses in Park Royal itself?

faq.a: It depends on the parcel, and the two can be streets apart. Municipal-side homes are freehold under District bylaws (Zoning 4662 / OCP 4985); lands on Capilano IR No. 5 are leasehold under the 1974 Park Royal Lease, with the Squamish Nation controlling zoning.
faq.q: Is a home near Park Royal freehold or leasehold?

faq.a: Any purchase there is a developer-contract (REDMA) purchase; the disclosure statement, not marketing copy, is where a townhome component's legal form would be settled.
faq.q: The Executive on the Park page mentions townhomes. Can I buy one as a townhouse?

faq.a: What sells here is a strata apartment condo at the centre, a whole detached house south of Marine Drive, or — on the reserve side — a leasehold interest, which is a different purchase entirely.
faq.q: Can I buy a half duplex at Park Royal?

faq.a: Both, depending on the parcel. The shopping centre and surrounding area sit at West Vancouver's eastern edge; part of the centre stands on Capilano Indian Reserve No. 5, Squamish Nation land held under the 1974 Park Royal Lease, where the Nation exercises zoning control. The two can be streets apart — tenure is confirmed on the individual title, never assumed from the sub-area name.
faq.q: Is Park Royal in West Vancouver or on First Nations land?

faq.a: Homes on the municipal side are freehold; homes on reserve land are leasehold, on the head-lease terms, remaining term and any prepaid/rent-reset structure. Run the tenure check first, before pricing or financing discussions.
faq.q: Are homes near Park Royal freehold?

faq.a: No. There is no strata lot and no Form B on a leasehold interest — the governing diligence is the head lease itself, and lenders treat reserve-land leaseholds individually, so flag the tenure to the mortgage broker at the offer stage.
